The Police Sub-Inspector of Yeshwanthpura Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 504, 323, 324 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
Accused namely Sri Manas dropped out from the charge sheet.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Smitha.R. and the accused No.1 was solemnized on 25-05-2022 as per Hindu customs and rites.

After the marriage, CW1 was residing at house No.326, 8th Cross, 12th Main, HMT Layout, Mattikere, within the limits of Yeshwanthpura Police Station, Bengaluru City with accused persons wherein the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention KABC030452742024 CC No.25940/2024 subjected the CW1 to mental and physical Smitha R vs Santhosh Kumar on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103340891/
2 cruelty.
Therefore, CW1 lived separately with the accused No.1 in the 3rd floor of the aforesaid building.

That being so, on 21-5-2024 at around 9.30 pm, accused No.2 picked up quarrel with CW1 and all accused persons with common intention abused CW1 with filthy language, had voluntarily beaten her with their hands and accused No.2 hit her with chapati making board (
  
) and caused simple injury to CW1.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1, the Sri Naveed, CW6/PSI of Yeshwanthpura Police Station registered Crime No.193/2024 against the accused No.1 to 5 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 504, 323, 324 read with Sec.34 IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court.

4. Investigation: Thereafter, he drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 on 25-05-2024, recorded the statements of requisite witnesses, collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the alleged offences by dropping accused namely Sri Manas from the charge sheet.
5.
On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offences alleged against the accused persons.
At pre-summoning stage, the accused No.1 and 3 to 5 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 27-05-2024.
At trial stage accused No.2 was enlarged on bail by the order dated 25-11-2024.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused persons.

8. Charge: After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused persons, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 504, 323, 324 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, has been framed, read over and explained to the accused persons in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9.
Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 6 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 2 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused No.1 have compromised the matrimonial differences between them and living together and hence the examination of CW2 to CW6 was dispensed with by the order dated 31-05-2025.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Smitha.R. with accused No.1 was residing at house No.326, 8th Cross, 12th Main, HMT Layout,
Mattikere, within the limits of Yeshwanthpura Police Station, with common intention subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offences punishable under KABC030452742024 CC No.25940/2024 Sec.498(A) read with Section 34 of IPC?
2.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that when CW1 lived separately with the accused No.1 in the 3rd floor of the above building, on 21-5-2024 at around 9.30 pm,
accused No.2 picked up quarrel with CW1 and accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention abused CW1 with filthy language, with filthiest language, knowingly such abusive words will provoke breach of peace thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.504 read with Section 34 of IPC?
3.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration,
accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention had voluntarily KABC030452742024 CC No.25940/2024 beaten CW1 with their hands and caused simple hurt to CW1 thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.323 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
4.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration,
accused No.2 in furtherance of common intention hit CW1 with chapati board (
  
  ) and caused simple injury thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.323 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
5. What order?

The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 to 4 : In the Negative Point No.5 : As per final order KABC030452742024 CC No.25940/2024 REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 4: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows:
i. CW1 by name Smt. Smitha.R., being informant examined as PW1 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2(Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a) and deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the minor differences of opinion amongst her and the accused No. 1, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 Smitha R vs Santhosh Kumar on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103340891/
4 and further stated that she did not lodge complaint against accused and no mahazar was conducted in her presence and she has not taken treatment with the history of assault.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

On perusal of aforesaid recitation, it is clear that the disputes between the accused No.1 and CW1 (informant) have been settled and they were living together.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat),
wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it KABC030452742024 CC No.25940/2024 became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A), 504, 323, 324 of IPC is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

sentences.text: 18. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.
Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and
hence the ingredients for offences Under Section 498(A)- 504, 323, 324 of IPC was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 4 in the Negative.

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 4, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 4 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 504, 323, 324 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) After the expiry of appeal period, the property shown under PF No.57/2024 shall be destroyed.
(v) Ordered accordingly.
